key_insight: X^3-OPD shows that an audio-language model can learn stronger reasoning by generating its own reasoning traces and aligning them with a text teacher, rather than relying only on scarce human-labeled audio reasoning data. The result is a cross-modal distillation method that transfers deep logic from text into audio understanding.
problem_solved: Large audio-language models can perceive sound well, but they still struggle with multi-step reasoning because high-quality audio reasoning data is limited. This paper addresses the data bottleneck by distilling reasoning ability from a powerful text model into an audio-language student.
method: Use a strong text-based teacher model to provide reasoning guidance.
Train the audio-language student with on-policy distillation, where it generates its own reasoning trajectories during training.
Align student outputs with teacher reasoning across modalities to improve logical inference in audio tasks.
impact: This matters because it offers a practical way to improve reasoning in audio-language systems without needing massive new annotated datasets. For practitioners, it suggests a scalable path to build more capable multimodal assistants for speech, sound-event analysis, and audio QA.

paper_title: X$^3$-OPD: Distilling Reasoning into Large Audio-Language Models via On-Policy Alignment
paper_authors: Dongjie Fu, Di Cao, Xize Cheng, Zihan Zhang, Wenxu Jia
